To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have synthesized diamond–silica composites with a variety of structures, including diamond–silica–silica nanotube, diamond–silica nanowire, and diamond–silica nanoparticle composites.

composites of diamond and one-dimensional (1-D) nanostructures can be synthesized by microwave plasma assisted chemical vapour deposition (MPCVCD) on 1-D nanostructured matrix seeded with diamond particles.

composites of nanocrystalline diamond and 1-D nanosilica can be synthesized by MPCVD, and that the composites are expected to be useful in many applications, e.g., as protective coatings for electronic devices, and for biomedical applications.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel approach for the preparation of diamond-tipped one dimensional nanostructure composite thin films.
synthesis of nanodiamond–1-D nanostructures composites by MPCVD.
the synthesis of novel nanodiamond-silica nanotube composite films and diamond crystals on silica nanotubes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the composites of diamond and 1-D silica nanostructures can be synthesized by means of MPCVD.

the nanodiamond–nanotube composite is a novel material with potential application as a high temperature, high power electronic device, a field emission cathode, a high temperature sensor, and a high power microwave device.
the nanodiamond–1D nanocomposite is a new class of materials with a combination of unique properties that are distinct from the individual components.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have successfully demonstrated a method for synthesizing diamond-tipped 1-D nanostructured materials by using nanodiamond particles as diamond seeds.
we have demonstrated a new method of fabricating 3-D nanostructured composites of nanosized diamond and 1-D nanosized silica tubes.
we have successfully developed a method to synthesize nanodiamond–1-D nanostructure composite thin films by using microwave plasma assisted chemical vapour deposition.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the composite thin films of nanoscale diamond and silica nanotube are promising materials for a number of potential applications, especially in nanoscale electronics and optoelectronics, as well as for biomedical applications.
nanodiamond can be used as a template for growth of other materials.
nanodiamond particles can be used to control and modify the surface properties of 1-D nanostructure-based composites.
